rubric.why: Gives the basic function of memory.
rubric.description: States that memory stores data or information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying memory as storage for data or information.

rubric.why: Shows what else memory holds or supports.
rubric.description: Mentions instructions, programs, or processing as part of memory’s role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to instructions, programs, or processing.

modelAnswer: Memory is the part of a computer that stores data and information.
It also holds instructions needed for processing.

items.followUp: Convert (101101)₂ into the decimal number system.

rubric.why: Shows the place-value expansion or the value of the highest binary digit.
rubric.description: Correctly identifies the place values used in the conversion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct place-value expansion or equivalent working.

rubric.why: The decimal conversion is the required result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final answer 65.

items.followUp: State one difference between RAM and ROM.

rubric.why: Identifies the defining data-retention property of volatile memory.
rubric.description: States that volatile memory loses its contents when power is switched off.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct effect of power loss on volatile memory.

rubric.why: Identifies the defining data-retention property of non-volatile memory.
rubric.description: States that non-volatile memory retains its contents when power is switched off.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct effect of power loss on non-volatile memory.

modelAnswer: Volatile memory loses its stored data when the power is switched off.
Non-volatile memory retains its data even when the power is switched off.

items.followUp: What are the two possible values of a Boolean variable?

rubric.why: Shows that truth values belong to logic or Boolean expressions.
rubric.description: Explains that truth values are values used in logic or Boolean expressions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying their logical or Boolean nature.

rubric.why: Names the two possible truth values.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark only when both values are stated.

modelAnswer: Truth values are the values that a logical or Boolean expression can have.

rubric.why: Identifies the unauthorized copying that constitutes piracy.
rubric.description: States that piracy involves unauthorized or illegal copying.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying unauthorized copying or reproduction.

rubric.why: Connects piracy to protected material or the lack of legal permission.
rubric.description: Mentions copyrighted material or copying without permission or a licence.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the protected material or missing permission/licence.

modelAnswer: Piracy is the illegal or unauthorized copying of copyrighted software or other protected material.
It is done without the permission of the copyright owner.

items.followUp: Give one example of a cyber crime.

rubric.why: Cyber crime must involve an offence or unlawful activity.
rubric.description: States that cyber crime is illegal or unlawful activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its illegal nature.

rubric.why: Identifies the computer or digital context of the crime.
rubric.description: Connects the illegal activity with computers, the internet, or a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the relevant digital means or environment.

modelAnswer: Cyber crime is an illegal activity carried out using a computer, the internet, or a computer network.

items.followUp: What does HTTP stand for, and what is it used for?

rubric.why: Gives the correct expansion of TCP.
rubric.description: Expands TCP as Transmission Control Protocol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct TCP expansion.

rubric.why: Gives the correct expansion of IP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct IP expansion.

modelAnswer: TCP/IP stands for Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol.
It is a set of protocols used for communication between computers over the internet.

items.followUp: Define a receiver in a communication system.

rubric.description: States that a message is information, data, or content.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the message as information or data.

rubric.why: Identifies the message’s role in communication.
rubric.description: States that the information is sent or transmitted from a sender to a receiver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the sender-to-receiver transmission.

modelAnswer: A message is the information or data sent from a sender to a receiver in a communication system.
